newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rashid gets regulator nod for restructure.
newsitem.headline: Rashid gets regulator nod for restructure.

text.p: Malaysian financial supermarket Rashid Hussain Bhd has received regulatory approval for its planned restructuring scheme, the national Bernama news agency said on Wednesday, quoting the company's merchant bank.
The approval came from the Securities Commission, which is the country's market watchdog.

The scheme, which involves the merger between Rashid Hussain's subsidiary DCB Holdings and Kwong Yik Bhd, both of which own commercial banks in Malaysia, was announced late in 1996. It is the biggest banking merger in Malaysia's history.

It added that the Commission had also approved a waiver to Rashid Hussain from having to undertake a mandatory general offer for the remaining shares in DCB Holdings not held by it upon completion of the proposals.

The merchant bank said Rashid Hussain and DCB Holdings also intended to change their financial year end from May 29 and Dec 31 respectively to June 30 so that the groups would have similar financial year ends.
